newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemenis negotiate with captors of French diplomat.
newsitem.headline: Yemenis negotiate with captors of French diplomat.

text.p: Yemeni security officials were negotiating the release of a French diplomat kidnapped by tribesmen in the Yemeni capital Sanaa on Monday, security sources said.

They did not have details on the diplomat, but said security forces were in negotiations with the al-Toaiman tribe, whose armed members abducted the diplomat while he was driving his car in a Sanaa street.
The sources, who earlier said the kidnappers took the diplomat to the province of Marib, 170 km (100 miles) north of Sanaa, said they were still trying to determine where he was being held.

The governor of Marib, Abdulwali al-Shamiri, told Reuters the diplomat's car had been spotted in Marib by local police before they were informed of his abduction. He said the police reported that the car had three passengers but were not sure the diplomat was among them.

"We are trying to determine the location of the kidnapped diplomat," he said. "Security forces are surrounding the village of al-Mahjaza in the area of the Toaiman tribe and negotiations, with the help of other tribes, are going on."
Deputy Interior Minister Colonel Taher al-Masri said efforts were still underway to determine the diplomat's whereabouts.
"We will deal firmly with them (the kidnappers)...But in a wise way until we secure his release," he told Reuters.
Another senior security official said security authorities planned "...to arrest members of the Toaiman tribe whether in Marib or Sanaa to put pressure on the kidnappers."
A French embassy official confirmed that a diplomat had been kidnapped, but refused to give any other details.

The Toaiman tribe earlier this month hijacked the car of Yemen's minister of agriculture and kidnapped his driver in Sanaa. The minister was not in the car at the time. The driver was beaten up and later set free.
The tribe demanded then that the government provide it with water pumps and drilling equipment for wells in Marib, 170 km (100 miles) north of Sanaa.
The security sources believed the tribe still has the same demands.
In recent years, tribes in Yemen with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped tourists or foreigners working in Yemen for use as bargaining chips.
At least two diplomats, an American and the Saudi ambassador, have been among the kidnap victims.
The tribes' demands have usually involved land or water issues, and have rarely been political. There have been no reports of casualties resulting from the abductions.
Some of the kidnap victims, mostly Westerners, were rescued by security forces. Others were set free, but it was never officially confirmed if any demands were met.
In January, members of a tribe kidnapped 17 elderly French tourists in Marib but released them later in the month.
